intended_object: The basis of R[X] (as a free R-module, indexed by ℕ) given by a polynomial sequence (S i of degree i) whose leading coefficients are all units. This comes from the docstring and module doc.
explanation:
The definition applies `Basis.mk` to two facts. The first is linear independence, which the file proves from right-regular leading coefficients; a unit is regular, so that hypothesis holds. The second is Mathlib's `Polynomial.Sequence.span`, which says the sequence spans all of R[X] when the leading coefficients are units. By `Basis.mk_apply`, the i-th basis vector is S i. That is the intended object.

On generality: Mathlib's `Polynomial.Sequence.basis` builds the same basis but needs `[IsDomain R]`. This definition only needs `[Ring R]`, so it is more general than Mathlib's version.

It cannot be pushed down to semirings, because spanning needs subtraction. Over ℕ, take the sequence 1, X+1, … (all leading coefficients are 1, a unit). X is not a combination of these with coefficients in ℕ, since X = (X+1) − 1 needs a negative coefficient. So rings are the right setting, and the definition is faithful.
